name: DaVinci Waveform Audio Sync In Media Pool
use_when: Camera footage has scratch audio and separate higher-quality production audio.
Video and audio share enough waveform detail for automatic sync.
A batch of interview, tutorial, or dialogue clips needs synced audio before editing.
avoid_when: Camera audio is missing or too noisy for waveform matching.
The external audio is from a different take or has drift that needs manual repair.
The camera audio is already final-quality and no replacement is needed.

timeline_pattern.batch_rule: Batch sync only when all selected clips have matching scratch/reference audio.
timeline_pattern.failure_rule: Mark failed syncs for manual sync instead of assuming silence or non-dialogue clips are safe.
timeline_pattern.replacement_rule: Confirm the good external audio replaced or linked correctly before muting scratch audio.

motion.rule: No direct motion rule; synced audio improves cut timing and action matching.

sound.rule: Use waveform sync as a starting point, then listen for one-sided channels, drift, bad replacement, or missing dialogue.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: For dialogue edits, audible lip-sync should be within a frame or two; manually repair obvious flams.
keyframe_values.channel_check: If a WAV imports as left-only or multi-channel, split or map channels before judging the sync.

captions.rule: Generate captions from the synced dialogue track, not from scratch camera audio when the external track is cleaner.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use waveform correlation or manual clap/timecode offsets, then store offsetSeconds per clip before muxing or timeline assembly.
implementation.remotion: Store externalAudioOffsetFrames and channelMap metadata for each clip.
implementation.blender: Align audio and video strips by waveform or clap marker, then lock or group them.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use auto sync or manually align waveform peaks, then mute/delete scratch audio only after playback review.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Synchronize clips by audio waveform, create merged/multicam clips where appropriate, and verify channel mapping.

common_mistakes: Batch syncing and never checking failed clips.
Deleting scratch audio before confirming the replacement track is correct.
Ignoring one-sided or multi-channel WAV import problems.
Generating captions from poor scratch audio after syncing better external audio.
qc: Did every intended clip show a successful sync or get marked for manual repair?
Does playback confirm lip sync and no doubled echo/flam?
Is dialogue centered or intentionally panned after channel mapping?
Were failed or non-dialogue sync attempts reviewed manually?
Are captions/transcripts based on the clean synced audio?
